newsitem.title: ITALY: Edison sees no need for capital rise.
newsitem.headline: Edison sees no need for capital rise.

text.p: Italian energy company Edison, part of the Montedison group, has no need for a capital increase and can cover investment costs with its own high profitability, managing director Giulio Del Ninno told the AGM.
"Edison has a high debt capacity with a debt equity ratio of 0.39 at end-1996, therefore it does not have any problem in taking investment opportunities," Del Ninno said.
Chairman Enrico Bondi also told shareholders, "Edison has up to now coped with investments autonomously with its own resources."
There has been some recent market talk of the private energy group carrying out a capital increase.
Edison plans investments of around 450 billion lire this year and slightly less for 1998.
